Rate is DB-backed config depositCommissionPct (0-100). Commission is integer minor units, rounded DOWN, clamped to the deposit amount, and idempotent on the deposit reference (idempotencyKey deposit-commission:{provider}:{reference}) so a retry/duplicate submit never double-pays. Ledger entryType 'agent_receipt', sourceType 'deposit_commission'. Agent self-performance (GET /agent/performance) and admin overview (GET /admin/agents/performance) now also report depositCount, depositVolumeMinor, depositCommissionEarnedMinor.

features.title: Authoritative M-PESA portal receipt verification (PDF)
features.behavior: Mirrors the Telebirr receipt fetch for M-PESA. The confirmation SMS links to https://m-pesabusiness.safaricom.et/receipt/<code>, a Next.js SPA that loads its data from GET /api/receipt/getReceipt?trxNo=<code> → { responseCode, responseDescription, base64Data } where base64Data is a receipt PDF. responseCode '0' proves the code is a REAL, settled transaction (a forged SMS code returns e.g. 2032 'does not exist'). The PDF text layer is UNMASKED — full sender/receiver name + phone, settled amount, payment date (EAT), transaction type — unlike the SMS which masks the counterparty (251714***707 vs real 251714267707). New MpesaReceiptClientService (leaf module) fetches the JSON (direct or via MPESA_PORTAL_URL proxy), decodes the base64 PDF, extracts text with pdf-parse, and parses it (pure parseMpesaReceiptText). Deposit verifier: when MPESA_PORTAL_ENABLED, the portal receipt is authoritative — confirms existence+success, settled amount == SMS amount, unmasked receiver == matched agent; hard-rejects conflicts and not-found; a portal OUTAGE falls back to SMS unless MPESA_PORTAL_STRICT. Withdrawal verifier: same authoritative path — unmasked receiver == player destination, settled amount == net payout; outage BLOCKS release (admin approve is the override).

features.behavior: There is no self-service admin sign-up endpoint, and POST /dev/seed/admin is disabled once NODE_ENV=production (DevController.guardProduction), so a brand-new production database has no way to get its first admin. New AdminBootstrapService (OnApplicationBootstrap, in UsersModule) reads ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_ACCOUNTS (JSON array of {phoneNumber, password, displayName}) and calls the new UsersService.ensureAdminAccount for each — creates a User (roles ['admin'], status 'active') + a password-provider AuthIdentity (argon2id hash) ONLY if no password identity already exists for that phone number. features.title: Fix repeated 'Round is running'/'Round is crashed' errors from multi-process Crash scheduler
features.behavior: Production error log showed CrashScheduler repeatedly failing to start the SAME round id every ~12s with alternating ConflictException('Round is running')/ConflictException('Round is crashed'). Root cause: CrashScheduler cached round phase/timing in process-local instance fields (activeRoundId, roundStatus, roundStartedAt, waitingStartedAt, crashPointX100), only updated by ITS OWN successful ticks. The Redis lock (CRASH_LOCK_KEY) only serializes a single tick's critical section across processes — it does not synchronize what different processes believe the current phase is. On a multi-process deployment (Phusion Passenger running >1 worker for the app), a process winning a LATER lock acquisition with stale/idle local memory would treat an already-in-flight round (created/advanced by ANOTHER process) as freshly created, arm its own local waiting-timer, and later race to start/settle a round another process already advanced — producing the observed errors indefinitely. Fixed by making CrashScheduler.runTick() re-derive phase and timing from the CrashRound DB row every tick (new CrashService.getActiveRoundEntity(), scheduler-internal only — exposes the real crashPointX100 even mid-round, unlike the public-safe getActiveRound()) instead of trusting cached fields; all local phase/timer instance fields and resetState() were removed. A ConflictException from startRound (another process won the race) is now an expected no-op, not a logged error. settleRound was already idempotent (a round already 'crashed' just returns instead of throwing) so no change needed there. ALSO hardened CrashService.abandonStaleRounds() (boot-time cleanup): it previously treated ANY non-crashed round as abandoned, which would let a newly-booting process (e.g. Passenger spinning up a new worker) wrongly refund live bets and crash a round that ANOTHER already-running process is legitimately still driving mid-round — a real financial-correctness bug, not just log noise. Now age-gated: a 'waiting' round is only abandoned past 5 minutes old, a 'running' round past 10 minutes (or with no startedAt at all) — both comfortably beyond any real round's lifetime (waitingDurationSeconds default 12s; even at maxMultiplierX100=10000 the exponential growth formula resolves in under 90s).

features.title: Agent referral codes (attribution-only) + mandatory agent location capture
features.behavior: Two related additions to agent->player attribution, both decided with the user before implementation. (1) REFERRAL CODES. Before this, `users.referredByAgentId` could only ever be set by PaymentsService when an agent processed a player's first credited deposit (payments.service.ts, guarded `WHERE referredByAgentId IS NULL`), so a player who signed up and played without an agent-handled deposit stayed permanently unattributed and a recruiting agent got no credit. Each agent now has a `users.referralCode` (nullable varchar(16) + UNIQUE index; MySQL allows many NULLs so existing rows don't collide) generated by `generateReferralCode` in the new src/common/referral-code.util.ts -- crypto.randomInt (not Math.random: codes are public and attribute customers), 6 chars from a confusable-safe alphabet that excludes O/0, I/1/L and U. Players arrive via a Telegram deep link `t.me/<bot>?start=ref_<code>`; the player bot's /start handler previously ignored its payload entirely, and now calls `captureReferralFromStart` BEFORE the already-onboarded early-return, so a returning-but-unattributed player following an agent's link still gets credited. Because a brand-new player has no `users` row at /start time (the account is created on contact-share) AND production runs multiple Passenger workers (so /start and the contact update can land on different processes -- the same multi-process reality that caused BE-BUG-01), the pending code is parked in REDIS (`referral:pending:<telegramUserId>`, 24h TTL) rather than an in-memory map, and `applyPendingReferral` consumes it in the contact handler once the account exists. `UsersService.attributeReferral` resolves code->agent and updates guarded by `id = :userId AND referredByAgentId IS NULL`, so first-attribution-wins and is never reassigned -- which means the referral code beats a later deposit by a different agent WITH ZERO CHANGES to the money path, because the existing deposit-linking query already carries the same IS NULL guard. Rejects self-referral, suspended/non-agent code owners, unknown codes, and malformed payloads (normalizeReferralCode only ever matches our own alphabet, so garbage never reaches a DB query). Per the user's explicit choice, referrals are ATTRIBUTION ONLY -- they feed `customersBrought`/area reporting/lobby highlighting and deliberately do NOT create a payout path (agent commission stays per-deposit and per-room); verified beforehand that `referredByAgentId` is read nowhere in bingo/wallet/ledger. New `GET /agent/referral` (@Roles('agent'), scoped off @CurrentUser so no agent can read another's code) returns `{ code, link, referredPlayers }`, generating the code on first access via `ensureAgentReferralCode` -- lazy generation is what backfills agents created before this feature, so no one-off migration script was needed. `link` is null when the new TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME env var is unset (code still returned so it can be shared manually). Frontend: a shared `ReferralCard` in components/AgentAreaViews.tsx (code, copy-to-clipboard with a graceful fallback for in-app webviews where navigator.clipboard is blocked, and a referred-player count) rendered atop the 'My Area' tab, so the web Agent page and the standalone agent-frontend both get it. (2) MANDATORY AGENT LOCATION. The agent bot previously had contact-share only. It now requires a location pin after linking and withholds the 'Open Agent Panel' button until one is shared (already-shared agents pass straight through). Crucially, and per an explicit AskUserQuestion decision, the pin is INFORMATIONAL ONLY: `UsersService.setAgentSharedLocation` writes new `users.sharedLatitude`/`sharedLongitude`/`sharedLocationAt` columns and NEVER touches `agent_locations`, so it cannot change which players an agent may see. Area visibility stays governed solely by admin-assigned `agent_locations` rows, because a Telegram pin is client-supplied and freely draggable -- auto-assigning from it would let any agent read another area's customer deposits/withdrawals by moving the map. The captured pin instead surfaces in the admin 'Assign Agents to Locations' panel as a Google Maps link + capture timestamp, so it speeds up assignment without granting anything. Unlike the player bot's location step there is no pick-from-list fallback (an agent's own coordinates are the point), and web credentials login remains available so a client that cannot send a pin never locks an agent out.

features.title: Fix agent-to-player transfer failing for national '09/07' phone format
features.behavior: Agent-to-player wallet transfers (POST /agent/wallet/transfer-to-user) silently returned 'User with phone number ... not found' whenever the agent typed the player's phone in national '09XXXXXXXX'/'07XXXXXXXX' form -- only the canonical '+2519XXXXXXXX'/'+2517XXXXXXXX' form worked. Root cause: WalletService.transferAgentToUser (wallet.service.ts) took the DTO-validated phone string and passed it STRAIGHT to `userRepo.findOneBy({ phoneNumber: userPhone })` with no normalization. The DTO's own @Matches regex (`/^(\+?251|0)[79]\d{8}$/`) happily accepts '09...' as valid input, so validation passed -- but every write path that sets a PLAYER's users.phoneNumber (setTelegramPhone, createAgentUser/ensureAdminAccount, updateAgentUser, updatePhoneByTelegramId) runs the value through normalizeEthiopianPhone first, so the column is always stored in canonical +251 form. An unnormalized '09...' lookup therefore never matched a real row, regardless of whether the player actually existed. Audited the rest of the codebase for the same pattern (grepped every phoneNumber-keyed user lookup) and confirmed this was the only occurrence; every other lookup (findBackofficeUserByCredentials, findAgentByPhone, etc.) already normalizes first. Fixed by normalizing userPhone via normalizeEthiopianPhone up front and throwing BadRequestException on an invalid input BEFORE opening the transaction (matching the style already used in createAgentUser/ensureAdminAccount), then looking up by the normalized value. The idempotency key and NotFoundException message were left using the raw input (harmless -- the key just needs to be stable per request, and echoing back what the agent actually typed is clearer than echoing a normalized form they didn't type).

features.title: Fix profile phone-number edit letting a player silently claim another player's phone number
features.behavior: Two live player accounts (BiniSoG, 10 ETB and Binyam B., 1000 ETB) were found sharing the exact same phoneNumber (+251713927296). Diagnosed to PATCH /users/me (UsersController.updateMe -> UsersService.updateProfile): the endpoint has only @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard) -- no @Roles restriction -- and updateProfile wrote `user.phoneNumber = normalizedPhone` with ZERO check for whether another account already held that number. The user confirmed the actual trigger: they edited their phone from the Mini App's Profile section while logged into a second/newer Telegram-linked account, typing in a phone number an existing older account already owned -- the write succeeded silently, with no verification of any kind that they actually owned that number. A diagnostic query (GROUP BY phoneNumber HAVING COUNT(*) > 1, scoped to role 'player') confirmed this was the only such pair in production, so it was an isolated incident rather than a widely-hit bug. Fixed by adding a conflict check in updateProfile: when the normalized phone differs from the account's current one, reject with ConflictException if another user with status='active' AND JSON_CONTAINS(roles, '"player"') already holds it. Deliberately scoped to role 'player' (not a global phoneNumber check) because users.phoneNumber is INTENTIONALLY allowed to repeat across DIFFERENT roles by design -- see BE-AGENT-01/BE-AGENT-02's multi-role-per-phone architecture, where an agent and a player (or admin and agent) may legitimately share one phone number as two separate accounts. A global uniqueness rule here would have broken that intentional feature. updatePhoneByTelegramId (a second write path with the identical missing-check pattern) was found to have zero callers anywhere in the codebase and was left untouched as dead code, not part of this fix.

Traced the cause: every User row, regardless of role, gets a personal Wallet lazily created via ensureDefaultWallet the first time GET /wallet is called, and neither WalletBar nor the Wallet.tsx page it links to were gated by role -- BottomNav already correctly hid its own wallet tab unless roles.includes('player'), but WalletBar had no equivalent check, so an admin's dormant personal wallet was fully reachable via the top bar. The Master Wallet code itself (AdminService.adminTopup) was already correct and required no receipt/proof, exactly as intended for injecting e-money supply. User's stated goal: 'strictly one wallet for admins... it should only be the ultimate source of the emoney.' That framing surfaced a second, more serious gap while investigating: POST /payments/telebirr/receipts, /payments/mpesa/receipts (and their /preview counterparts), and POST /wallet/withdraw had NO role restriction -- only JwtAuthGuard -- and credit/debit whoever is authenticated (@CurrentUser()). features.title: Master Wallet becomes the ONLY source of e-money — every other credit is now funded from it, not minted
features.behavior: Following BE-BUG-04 (Master Wallet as the ONE admin-visible balance), the user pushed further: 'everything should flow according to the master wallet' -- i.e. the Master Wallet should be the ONLY place e-money is created, not just the only thing admins see. Audited every walletService.creditInSession/.credit() call site in the codebase (grepped all of src) to find every credit with no corresponding debit anywhere ('minting'). Found four genuine production mint paths, confirmed with the user via AskUserQuestion (scope: 'all four'; insufficient-Master-Wallet-balance behavior: 'block the credit until admin tops up', not allow-negative): (1) PaymentsService.submitTelebirrReceipt/submitMpesaSms crediting the player directly for a verified real-money deposit; (2) PaymentsService.creditAgentDepositCommission minting the agent's deposit commission; (3) AdminService.adjustUserWallet's credit direction (the debit direction was ALSO changed, see below, though not explicitly asked -- symmetry/conservation); (4) AuthService's welcome-bonus grant on first login. Explicitly audited and confirmed OUT of scope, i.e. correctly left as pure redistribution rather than new mints: every Bingo/Keno/Crash/Pool/Werk win/refund/stake credit (pays out of an already-collected pot, zero-sum), and WalletService's withdrawal-settlement agent/service-fee split (netAmountMinor + commissionMinor + serviceFeeMinor sums exactly back to the player's already-reserved withdrawal.amountMinor -- a redistribution of money the Master Wallet already funded at deposit time, not a new mint). Also found but NOT changed pending a separate decision: SupportService.approveRefundRequest (same category as admin adjustment -- discretionary credit, no backing) and BotsService's house-bot initial/top-up funding (fake AI-player bankroll, arguably a different category -- game-economy tuning rather than real customer e-money); both flagged to the user as follow-ups, not silently included or excluded. Design: new AdminService.creditFromMasterWallet(input, manager) is the SINGLE mechanism through which e-money now enters any wallet other than the Master Wallet itself -- debits the Master Wallet (entryType: 'adjustment', sourceType:'master_wallet_funding') then credits the target with the CALLER's original entryType/sourceType/sourceId/idempotencyKey/metadata unchanged (so existing ledger history/reporting semantics for the receiving wallet are identical to before), all within the CALLER's own EntityManager/transaction -- never a nested transaction. debitInSession's pre-existing insufficient-balance check (ConflictException) does the blocking automatically: if it throws, the whole caller transaction rolls back (e.g. the TelebirrDeposit row never gets persisted at all if the Master Wallet can't cover it), and creditFromMasterWallet re-throws a GENERIC message ('Unable to process this right now...') rather than leaking the words 'Master Wallet' to a player or agent. Companion method debitToMasterWallet(input, manager) is the reverse -- debits a wallet and returns the amount to the Master Wallet (entryType:'adjustment', sourceType:'master_wallet_reclaim') -- used for adjustUserWallet's debit direction, so money REMOVED from a player by an admin correction returns to the Master Wallet instead of vanishing from the ledger, keeping total system supply conserved either way; this direction was a judgment call (not explicitly requested) made for consistency with the 'Master Wallet is the ultimate source' principle, and is called out clearly so the user can redirect it if unwanted. All four call sites (PaymentsService x2 deposit credits, x1 shared commission helper used by both providers, AdminService.adjustUserWallet both directions, AuthService welcome bonus) needed zero new module wiring -- PaymentsModule, AdminService itself, and AuthModule already had AdminService/each other injected. The welcome-bonus call site already had a try/catch specifically commented 'Never let a welcome-bonus hiccup block login' -- that pre-existing safety net transparently absorbs a Master-Wallet shortfall too, with zero new special-casing needed.
